::: {.page-banner}
# Interactive Simulations
:::

::: {.section}
::: {.container}

These interactive simulations help students visualize core ideas in **probability**, **statistics**, **linear algebra**, and **machine learning**. They are designed for classroom demonstrations, self-study, and exploratory learning.

Use this page as a teaching hub: students can first review the concept in lecture, then open a simulation, change parameters, observe patterns, and connect the visual behavior back to formulas and theory.

::: {.buttons}
[Probability](#probability-theory){.button .primary}
[Statistics](#statistics){.button .secondary}
[Linear Algebra](#linear-algebra){.button .secondary}
[Machine Learning](#machine-learning){.button .secondary}
:::

::: {.highlight .sim-note}
### File location note

This QMD file is intended to live inside the `Teaching/` folder. Each simulation link uses the relative path `simulations/filename.html`, and each preview image uses the relative path `simulations/images/filename.svg` or `simulations/images/filename.png`.
:::

:::
:::

## Probability Theory

::: {.section}
::: {.container}

Probability theory becomes more intuitive when students can repeatedly simulate random experiments and compare empirical behavior with theoretical predictions.

::: {.grid}

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/clt-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/simulation-preview-images.svg" alt="Central Limit Theorem preview"></a>

### Central Limit Theorem

Explore how the distribution of sample means approaches a normal distribution as the sample size increases, regardless of the original population distribution.

[View Simulation](simulations/clt-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/monte-carlo-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/monte-carlo-preview.svg" alt="Monte Carlo pi estimation preview"></a>

### Monte Carlo $\pi$ Estimation

Use random sampling to estimate $\pi$ by generating points in a square and counting how many fall inside an inscribed circle.

[View Simulation](simulations/monte-carlo-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/monty-hall-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/monty-hall-preview.svg" alt="Monty Hall simulation preview"></a>

### Monty Hall Problem

Test the famous probability puzzle and compare the long-run winning rates for switching versus staying with the original choice.

[View Simulation](simulations/monty-hall-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/buffons_needle_simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/buffons-needle-preview.svg" alt="Buffon's Needle preview"></a>

### Buffon's Needle

Estimate $\pi$ by dropping random needles on parallel lines and observing the crossing frequency.

[View Simulation](simulations/buffons_needle_simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/cauchy_distribution_demo.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/cauchy-distribution-preview.svg" alt="Cauchy distribution preview"></a>

### Cauchy Distribution

Visualize how a random angle transformation can produce the heavy-tailed Cauchy distribution.

[View Simulation](simulations/cauchy_distribution_demo.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/hypergeometric-urn-experiment.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/hypergeometric-urn-preview.svg" alt="Hypergeometric urn experiment preview"></a>

### Hypergeometric Urn Experiment

Study sampling without replacement from a finite population and compare simulated outcomes with the hypergeometric distribution.

[View Simulation](simulations/hypergeometric-urn-experiment.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/rat_three_door_maze_with_visual.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/maze.png" alt="Rat in a maze preview"></a>

### Rat in a Three-Door Maze

Use conditional expectation and Monte Carlo simulation to analyze the expected time for a rat to exit a three-door maze.

[View Simulation](simulations/rat_three_door_maze_with_visual.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/negative_binomial_sim.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/negative-binomial-preview.svg" alt="Negative binomial simulation preview"></a>

### Negative Binomial Simulation

Model the number of failures before reaching a fixed number of successes in independent Bernoulli trials.

[View Simulation](simulations/negative_binomial_sim.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/bayesian-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/bayesian-preview.svg" alt="Bayesian coin flip preview"></a>

### Bayesian Coin Flip

See how Bayesian inference updates beliefs about a coin's fairness as additional flips are observed.

[View Simulation](simulations/bayesian-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

:::
:::
:::

## Statistics

::: {.section}
::: {.container}

These simulations support statistical reasoning by showing sampling variability, confidence, hypothesis testing, experimental comparison, and model assumptions.

::: {.grid}

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/confidence-interval-sim.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/confidence-interval-preview.svg" alt="Confidence interval simulation preview"></a>

### Confidence Interval Simulation

Generate repeated confidence intervals and observe the long-run coverage behavior relative to the true population mean.

[View Simulation](simulations/confidence-interval-sim.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/hypothesis-test-sim.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/hypothesis-test-preview.png" alt="Hypothesis testing simulation preview"></a>

### Hypothesis Testing Simulation

Visualize critical regions, test statistics, $p$-values, Type I error, Type II error, and power.

[View Simulation](simulations/hypothesis-test-sim.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/ab-testing-sim.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/ab-testing-preview.svg" alt="A/B testing simulation preview"></a>

### A/B Testing Simulation

Compare control and treatment variants, study lift, confidence intervals, statistical significance, and power analysis.

[View Simulation](simulations/ab-testing-sim.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/gamblers-ruin-example.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/gambler_ruin.png" alt="Gambler's ruin simulation preview"></a>

### Gambler's Ruin Problem

Simulate a gambler's random walk until ruin or success and compare with theoretical absorption probabilities.

[View Simulation](simulations/gamblers-ruin-example.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/anova-assumptions-demo.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/anova-preview.svg" alt="ANOVA assumptions simulation preview"></a>

### One-Way ANOVA Assumptions

Explore normality, homogeneity of variance, and independence in the context of one-way ANOVA.

[View Simulation](simulations/anova-assumptions-demo.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/anova-sim.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/anova-preview.svg" alt="ANOVA simulation preview"></a>

### ANOVA Simulation

Generate group data, run ANOVA, inspect effect size, and connect between-group and within-group variation.

[View Simulation](simulations/anova-sim.html){.button .primary}
:::

:::

## Linear Algebra

::: {.section}
::: {.container}

Linear algebra is especially visual: matrices transform geometry, eigenvectors reveal stable directions, singular values organize information, and Markov chains describe long-run structure.

::: {.grid}

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/matrix-transformations-2d.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/matrix-transformations-preview.svg" alt="2D matrix transformations preview"></a>

### 2D Matrix Transformations

Visualize how matrices rotate, scale, shear, reflect, and project shapes in the plane.

[View Simulation](simulations/matrix-transformations-2d.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/eigenvector-pca.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/pca-visualization-preview.png" alt="Principal component analysis preview"></a>

### Principal Component Analysis

Generate two-dimensional data, compute principal components, and visualize eigenvectors as directions of maximum variance.

[View Simulation](simulations/eigenvector-pca.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/svd-image-compression.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/svd-compression-preview.svg" alt="SVD image compression preview"></a>

### SVD Image Compression

Use singular value decomposition to compress an image and observe the tradeoff between rank, compression, and retained structure.

[View Simulation](simulations/svd-image-compression.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/markov-chain-pagerank.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/markov-pagerank-preview.png" alt="Markov chains and PageRank preview"></a>

### Markov Chains and PageRank

Explore random walks, transition matrices, stationary distributions, and PageRank values on directed graphs.

[View Simulation](simulations/markov-chain-pagerank.html){.button .primary}
:::

:::
:::
:::

## Machine Learning

::: {.section}
::: {.container}

These simulations connect algorithms to geometry, optimization, statistical learning, and neural-network computation.

::: {.grid}

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/linear-regression-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/linear-regression-preview.svg" alt="Linear regression simulation preview"></a>

### Linear Regression

Generate noisy data, fit a line, and understand residuals, least squares, fitted slope, intercept, and $R^2$.

[View Simulation](simulations/linear-regression-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/linear_regression_demo.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/linearGD.png" alt="Gradient descent simulation preview"></a>

### OLS vs Gradient Descent

Compare the closed-form ordinary least squares solution with iterative gradient descent for linear regression.

[View Simulation](simulations/linear_regression_demo.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/kmeans-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/kmeans-preview.svg" alt="K-means clustering preview"></a>

### K-Means Clustering

Watch the K-means algorithm iteratively assign points to clusters and update centroids until convergence.

[View Simulation](simulations/kmeans-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/bias_variance_simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/bias-variance-preview.svg" alt="Bias-variance tradeoff preview"></a>

### Bias-Variance Tradeoff

Study how model complexity, noise, and sample size affect bias, variance, and prediction error.

[View Simulation](simulations/bias_variance_simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/neural-network-simulation.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/neural-network-preview.svg" alt="Neural network training preview"></a>

### Neural Network Training

Observe a small neural network learn the XOR function through forward propagation, backpropagation, and gradient descent.

[View Simulation](simulations/neural-network-simulation.html){.button .primary}
:::

::: {.card .sim-card}
<a class="simulation-thumb-link" href="simulations/convolution_demo.html"><img class="simulation-thumb" src="simulations/images/CNN.png" alt="Neural network convolution visualizer preview"></a>

### Neural Network Convolution Visualizer

Watch how convolutional filters move across input data and transform it into feature maps.

[View Simulation](simulations/convolution_demo.html){.button .primary}
:::

## Suggested classroom use

::: {.section}
::: {.container}

::: {.two-col}

::: {.card}
### Before class

Ask students to open one simulation and predict what will happen when a parameter changes. For example, before discussing the Central Limit Theorem, ask what happens when sample size increases.
:::

::: {.card}
### During class

Use the simulation as a live demonstration. Pause after each run and connect the visual output to definitions, formulas, and assumptions.
:::

::: {.card}
### After class

Assign a short reflection: students should change two parameters, record what changed, and explain the result mathematically.
:::

::: {.card}
### For projects

Students can extend a simulation, add a new distribution, modify an algorithm, or compare empirical results with theoretical predictions.
:::

:::

:::
:::
